active.title: Publish the self-sufficient skills as Agent Skills packages on every harness channel
active.description: Adoption channel: distribution in 2026 is the marketplace, and the Claude marketplace alone is not viable because we support Codex and Kimi Code. The Agent Skills open standard (agentskills.io, 45+ adopters) IS cross-harness: Codex reads .agents/skills, Kimi Code reads .agents/skills, Claude Code reads it via plugin or `--add-dir`, and `npx skills add <repo>` installs into any of them. Publish the skills that survive without the workspace (dd-grill-me, dd-bug-resolution, dd-code-review three-axis, dd-test-stewardship) as one skills repo in the standard layout, registered on the Anthropic marketplace (claude-plugins-official / claude-community), the Codex marketplace (`codex marketplace add`) and installable by `npx skills add`; each skill names dadaia-workspace as the place where the full lifecycle lives. Complements plugin-packaging-and-skill-evals (the whole AI surface as one Claude plugin): this entry is the harness-neutral entry door.

active.title: Public presence: docs site, 5-minute quickstart, one video, Show HN, awesome-list PRs
active.description: Discoverability is zero: 1 star, 0 forks, 0 independent mentions; PyPI is the only channel; search engines return repo PRs before the README; 418 lines of docs for 55 commands. Deliver: a docs site (quickstart in 5 minutes, the bug -> RED -> fix -> resolve loop, and the page 'your product repos never carry agent config, one law governs ten projects'); one short video of the flow; a Show HN post; PRs to awesome-claude-code, awesome-agents.md and awesome-spec-driven-development; one article on the 512-record bug ledger and what it taught about fixes that breed bugs. Always promote the full slug 'dadaia-workspace' (the bare word collides with unrelated content). Gated on one-line-bootstrap, english-only-surface and the ceremony reduction: launching the product as it is invites the BMAD critique.

active.title: Hook derivation study: every hook is the per-harness implementation of a deterministic behavior the workspace defines; design the derivation for Claude, Codex, Kimi, Cursor, Devin, Copilot
active.description: Doctrine (operator, 2026-09-20): a hook never exists on its own; the rule is the abstract entity — a deterministic behavior the workspace enforces (root whitelist, venv guard, SDD gate, session-start reaper, context injection) — and each harness gets that rule's implementation in its own hook format (Claude settings.json, Codex hooks.json, Kimi [[hooks]] in user config.toml, Cursor hooks.json, Devin hooks.v1.json, Copilot .github/hooks/*.json). Study: one rule registry -> one renderer per harness; which harnesses fire hooks headless (Codex does not); which support project-level hooks (Kimi and ZCode: user-level only); the Claude-hooks bridge DeepSeek dsh ships. Not this cycle.
